skip_reason: Not a sales call — Landon is the customer here, not the rep. This is an outbound IT/vendor support call into a fleet-telematics provider (transcribed as 'Sara'/'Samar', almost certainly Samsara) about a gateway device that did not appear in the Einstein dashboard after activation. It opens with the vendor's own IVR and virtual agent ('Thank you for calling Sara... Hi, this is Annie sams virtual agent. How can I help you today?'), Landon states his issue ('I have a new gateway that I just tried to upload and it said it should be there, like it should have populated but it hasn't'), authenticates with his own work email ('Landon von @einsteinmoving.com'), gets triaged, and is transferred to a human specialist ('Thank you for calling Sara. My name is hope, how can I help you?') who walks him to Settings > Devices and finds the device was hidden behind a tag filter. Every direction of the sales scorecard is inverted: no Einstein prospect on the line, no move details, no quote, no pricing, no booking. The sales rubric does not apply. Note for the pipeline: the speaker labels are also unreliable on this record — the '(415) 329-6900' channel carries two different vendor-side voices (the virtual agent and then 'Hope'), so any automated attempt to score it would grade the vendor's script as if it were Landon's.
top_strength: Not gradeable, but Landon was an efficient and pleasant caller on the other side of the desk. He gave the vendor a complete, specific problem statement including the evidence and the elapsed time in one pass — 'I got an email from Sam saying your device activation is completed. One device has successfully activated and should... appear in your dashboard within ten minutes and that was three hours ago' — which is exactly what lets a support agent skip the discovery loop. He spelled his email and the serial number phonetically without being asked, self-corrected clearly when the agent checked a digit ('C. As in cat, like kitten or Kitty, like Kitty cat'), and when the fix turned out to be a tag filter he took it graciously rather than defensively: 'I'm sorry to even kind of waste your time with that. I think I could have figured that one out myself. Well, thank you so much for your help.' The agent reciprocated warmly, and the call closed on both sides wishing each other a good evening.
coaching_note: No sales coaching applies — this is a vendor support call with Landon as the caller. The actionable item is a pipeline one, not a rep one: this call reached the grading queue because it was on Landon's Dialpad line, and it should be filtered out before it dilutes his and the Dallas branch's averages. Two cheap filters would have caught it: (1) the leading turn is a vendor IVR disclosure ('This call is being recorded for quality assurance and training purposes'), meaning Einstein is the callee, not the caller — a strong skip signal; and (2) the transcript contains zero move-domain vocabulary (no address, no home size, no move date, no hourly rate). Worth adding an outbound-vendor pattern to the candidate-pull step so manager lines stop generating these. If Landon's Dialpad ID is going to keep surfacing non-sales traffic, that is also a reason to confirm whether a manager line belongs in the grading roster at all.
phone_presence_notes: Assessed only as caller courtesy since the sales rubric does not apply — Landon was clear, patient through two rounds of authentication and a transfer, and closed with genuine warmth ('I appreciate your help a lot... Awesome. You too, bye').
